title: Security review: Admin telemetry evidence pack and retention w/ Stellaris Health
summary: Redwood walked through the admin telemetry/evidence pack available to enterprise customers. Covered what events are logged (admin actions, role changes, API key use, login attempts, inference request metadata but prompt text redaction by default), export integrations (S3 export, Kafka stream, webhook/SIEM connectors), retention defaults (90 days), options for extended retention and cold archive, legal hold/forensic export process, and support for customer-managed KMS/HSM. Customer concerned about health-data residency and proof artifacts for upcoming SOC 2 audit. Next steps: share SOC 2 evidence checklist, sample export of 30 days of admin events, and paper on KMS rotation.
next_steps: Jordan to share SOC 2 evidence checklist and link to admin telemetry docs (by 2025-11-03)
Meera to provision a one-off 30-day export sample and upload link (by 2025-11-05)
Elliot to schedule a follow-up demo of SIEM integration with Splunk (by 2025-11-10)
action_items: Jordan: share SOC2 evidence checklist and confluence links (due 2025-11-03)
Meera: generate 30-day admin events export sample and provide S3 link (due 2025-11-05)
Luis: create short doc on KMS customer-managed key flows and rotation (due 2025-11-07)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: ok everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time today. we're going to focus on the admin telemetry evidence pack and retention. Meera will take most of the demo but i'll jump in for the compliance bits.
00:18 Dr. Ana Rivera: thanks, Jordan. baseline question — for our SOC 2 audit we need a tamper-evident trail of admin actions, and we need to show retention controls and exportability. can you confirm what's captured exactly?
00:32 Meera Patel: yeah great question. short answer: admin API and Console actions are logged — user create/delete, role assignment changes, policy updates, token/api key lifecycle events, login attempts (successful and failed), and importantly model deployments and version rollouts. we also log route-level config changes and can correlate them to the token that made the change.
01:02 Tom Brooks: when you say "token" do you mean API keys plus SSO sessions? how are SSO events surfaced?
01:12 Meera Patel: SSO assertions are captured as auth events: SAML/OKTA exchange result, user ID, timestamp, and the provider's IDP assertion id. we don't store raw SAML asserts, but we store enough metadata to link an auth session to actions.
01:30 Priya Shah: what about prompt text / inference payloads — any PII there? we can't have patient info retained.
01:38 Meera Patel: by default Redwood redacts full prompt/response bodies from admin telemetry. the admin events include inference metadata like model id, token counts, latency, and request hash. for enterprise agreements we can enable optional hashed payload retention or a secure payload store with customer-managed KMS, but that is controlled and must be agreed to.
02:05 Dr. Ana Rivera: ok, excellent. we need to show evidence that a given admin changed RBAC role X on 2025-09-20 and the event hasn't been altered. how do you provide tamper-proofing?
02:18 Luis Ortega: logs are stored in an append-only store with versioning and checksums — we also provide signed export bundles (evidence pack) that include the event stream, a manifest and a signature generated with our service key; for enterprise private deployments we support customer-provided HSM-backed signing.
02:40 Elliot Chen: is that signature stuff documented? auditors will want the exact chain of custody.
02:46 Jordan Lee: yes, we'll share a SOC 2 evidence checklist and the chain-of-custody doc. Meera will also generate a sample signed export.
03:00 Meera Patel: moving onto export options: we have native S3 exports (push to customer bucket), streaming exports to Kafka (TLS + SASL), and a webhook/SIEM connector that can push events to Splunk/Datadog/QRadar. exports can be full event JSON or compressed CSV manifest depending on your SIEM.
03:29 Tom Brooks: for S3 push, who writes to the bucket? do we give you credentials or you write via assume-role?
03:36 Meera Patel: we support two patterns: 1) cross-account assume-role where Redwood assumes a minimal-write IAM role in your AWS account; 2) we can push to a pre-signed URL provided by you. cross-account assume-role is recommended for continuous streaming export.
03:52 Priya Shah: retention defaults? our policy is 2 years for admin trails, but we were told your default is shorter.
03:59 Meera Patel: default hosted retention is 90 days for full event data. retention tiers: 90d hot, 1 year warm (aggregate indexes only), and enterprise cold-archive where we can keep full raw events for up to 7 years behind a reserved retention contract. private deployments you can set arbitrary retention in config.
04:26 Dr. Ana Rivera: are there e-discovery / legal hold capabilities if we need to retain certain records beyond retention?
04:33 Luis Ortega: yes, we support legal holds. you can flag a query or a set of principals and the platform will mark matching events as preserved — they are excluded from automated deletion and a preservation index is created. we will also produce a forensics bundle on request.
04:52 Elliot Chen: performance impact? if we enable long-term raw payload retention and signing, does that blow up our cost or latency?
04:58 Meera Patel: payload retention mostly affects storage cost; signing is async and doesn't add request latency. there is some CPU overhead for hashing at ingest, but negligible for typical throughput. if you need real-time signing we can discuss dedicated signing workers under Dedicated or Private deployments.
05:20 Priya Shah: KMS. we need customer key control. can you support CMKs? rotation? audit of key usage?
05:27 Luis Ortega: yes, we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and BYO-HSM options. key usage logs are recorded in the evidence pack — every decryption/encryption call will be correlated to the admin event and we provide an audit of key IDs used. key rotation is supported: new keys are used for new writes and we maintain decryption access to older objects per your retention.
05:51 Dr. Ana Rivera: how about export of key usage logs for auditor review?
05:55 Jordan Lee: we'll include a key-usage CSV in the evidence pack. Luis will include sample entries in the sample export.
06:05 Tom Brooks: data residency — our workloads for PHI must remain inside US-east. do you support regional isolation of logs?
06:13 Meera Patel: yes. Hosted regions store logs in-region. for stronger guarantees you should consider Dedicated or Private where we run the telemetry store inside your VPC or customer data center.
06:25 Priya Shah: can you demonstrate an actual evidence pack? show me how it's structured.
06:30 Meera Patel: sure. i'm going to share my screen — but quick note: the pack is a gzipped bundle that includes: events.jsonl (newline json events), manifest.json (range, sha256 checksums per file), signature.sig, index.csv (summary rows), and an assertions.txt that maps queries to filters.
07:02 Meera Patel: (screen) example event: {"ts":"2025-09-20T14:12:03Z", "actor":"u-1234", "event":"role.change", "target":"role:admin", "source":"console", "request_id":"r-9876"} — note this is a sanitized view; internal event has additional fields.
07:32 Dr. Ana Rivera: are user display names included or just IDs? auditors want both sometimes.
07:37 Meera Patel: by default we store user id and login; for PII minimization we do not store freeform display names unless configured. you can enable expanded identity enrichments for audit runs.
07:48 Priya Shah: do you retain logs of deleted users? if a user is deleted does the user id remain in the event history?
07:54 Luis Ortega: yes, events are immutable. identity attributes at the time-of-event are snapshot into the event; if you delete a user later, the historical events still have the snapshot.
08:10 Elliot Chen: ok curious about timelines — if we request an export for the last 30 days, how fast is that?
08:15 Meera Patel: for a 30-day admin event export under typical volume it should be ready within 24 hours; for large orgs we provide a staged export with a manifest and staged S3 objects.
08:28 Tom Brooks: does the export include diffs for config changes? auditors like to see before/after.
08:33 Meera Patel: yes, for config change events we store before/after snapshots and the delta is included in the event payload.
08:40 Dr. Ana Rivera: how do you handle chained actions — say an automation made a change on behalf of user X — is that attribution preserved?
08:45 Meera Patel: we include actor.type (human|service) and actor.origin (api|console|job) plus the originating request_id chain. chains are preserved when available.
08:55 Priya Shah: we also need to show RBAC permission grant history for a particular role. is there a query language?
09:02 Meera Patel: there is an audit query UI and an API; you can query by event type, actor, target, time-range, and freeform text. we will share examples of queries for RBAC history.
09:15 Jordan Lee: interrupt — a common mis-say: KV cache, K-V cache, might be transcribed weird in the notes but the events are proper.
09:22 Tom Brooks: haha noted.
09:25 Meera Patel: moving on SIEM integrations. any preference? you mentioned Splunk earlier.
09:30 Elliot Chen: yes Splunk, and we're piloting Elastic SIEM.
09:34 Meera Patel: Splunk: we can push HEC events, either directly or via your ingest cluster. Elastic: use Kafka or syslog. for QRadar/others we'll use the webhook connector. events include a severity mapping and standardized schema.
09:50 Priya Shah: encryption at-rest and in-transit — are there exceptions?
09:55 Luis Ortega: in-transit is TLS 1.2+ required. at-rest encryption is default and can be CMK-backed. we also offer field-level encryption for specific sensitive payloads.
10:10 Dr. Ana Rivera: for SOC 2 evidence they want to see testable controls — can you point us to a playbook of exactly which queries to run and what artifacts to present?
10:20 Jordan Lee: yes that's the evidence checklist I mentioned. it maps control IDs to artifacts: e.g., CC6.1 -> signed export for user provisioning changes; CC7.3 -> SIEM stream showing failed login attempts aggregated. we'll send that over.
10:34 Meera Patel: quick demo: i'm running a query for actor=u-1223 and event=role.change from 2025-09-01..2025-09-30. results: 12 events. showing the manifest for the export and the signature verification command we provide (we publish the public key).
11:00 Dr. Ana Rivera: what about detection of unusual admin activity? any built-in alerts?
11:06 Meera Patel: yes, Redwood Console supports rule-based alerts (geolocation, impossible travel, bulk role grants) and you can forward alerts to PagerDuty or Slack. we also provide anomaly-detection as an add-on.
11:24 Tom Brooks: logging levels — can we increase verbosity temporarily for an incident?
11:28 Meera Patel: yes there is a debug mode for a tenant; it's gated and auditable and should be used sparingly. logs generated in debug mode are flagged in the evidence pack.
11:41 Priya Shah: export integrity verification — auditors will run the verify command. show me exact steps.
11:46 Meera Patel: verification steps: download bundle, run redwood-verify --bundle path/to/bundle which will validate checksums, validate signature against published key, and output a manifest with matched query parameters. we will provide a Docker image for verification that auditors can run offline.
12:10 Elliot Chen: about retention policies per role — can we have retention tags per dataset? for example, admin events older than 1 year for default admin users but 7 years for HIPAA-related roles.
12:22 Luis Ortega: yes on Private/Dedicated you can set retention policies by tag or by event type. on hosted we support policy-based retention in the enterprise tier (tag-based retention for groups of events).
12:36 Dr. Ana Rivera: multi-tenant concerns — we need assurance that other customers' logs can't be mixed in.
12:42 Jordan Lee: strict tenancy boundaries, separate indices. for hosted, we logically separate, and evidence packs are tenant-scoped. Dedicated/Private gives physical isolation.
12:55 Priya Shah: are there demo artifacts we can attach to our SOC 2 binder?
13:00 Jordan Lee: yes, we'll provide the signed export sample, the verification Docker image, the SOC2 evidence checklist, and the KMS key usage csv. I'll put them in a shared folder.
13:12 Meera Patel: quick note: some fields in the event may be redacted in the sample. for a full run we need a data access agreement.
13:22 Dr. Ana Rivera: understood.
13:25 Tom Brooks: any limits on how far back we can query in the UI?
13:29 Meera Patel: UI is optimized for 90 days; longer-range queries hit our archive tier which may take longer and are accessed via export API.
13:38 Elliot Chen: customers sometimes worry about the operator level access inside Redwood — who can access the raw telemetry?
13:45 Luis Ortega: operator access is tightly controlled. access to raw telemetry is restricted to a small SRE on-call team and requires approvals, access is logged and included in the audit trail. for enterprise contracts we can do an arrangement where Redwood engineers do not have access and support runs via redacted artifacts — or run support sessions into your private deployment.
14:10 Priya Shah: license plate moment — do you support immutable S3 retention (object lock) on exports?
14:15 Meera Patel: yes if we write to your bucket we can set object-lock governance mode and retention tags as requested.
14:22 Dr. Ana Rivera: around compliance — you said you have SOC 2 and ISO? can you confirm scope and date?
14:28 Jordan Lee: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II through 2025-06 and ISO 27001 cert valid with scope covering the hosted platform; we'll share the compliance pack and the statement of applicability.
14:42 Priya Shah: vendor risk — do you run third-party penetration tests and share results?
14:47 Jordan Lee: we run annual pentests and remediation; summary reports are shared under an NDA.
14:55 Meera Patel: (brief) quick sidebar: there's a note in our docs about event name variations — sometimes "role.grant" might be transcribed as "role dot grant" in older exports; new exporters use canonical names.
15:08 Tom Brooks: ok this is useful. curious: can we see a small runbook for auditor queries?
15:14 Jordan Lee: yes we'll include runbook examples — we'll attach a CSV of canonical queries mapped to control IDs.
15:22 Meera Patel: i'm going to demo a signed evidence pack download — initiating now.
15:30 (screen) download started, package size 12MB for 30 days. manifest shows 3 files, sha256 checksums present. signature verified locally.
15:58 Dr. Ana Rivera: good. can we request a time-limited access token to review the bundle?
16:04 Meera Patel: yes we can create a pre-signed download link with 7-day validity or we can push it into your S3.
16:12 Priya Shah: for our SOC 2 timeline we need artifacts by 2025-11-20. is that feasible?
16:18 Jordan Lee: yes — Meera's export by 11/05 and the evidence pack + checklist by 11/03 should give you time.
16:26 Elliot Chen: one more technical: are logs idempotent? duplicates?
16:31 Meera Patel: events are de-duplicated by request_id and ingestion id; duplicates are annotated in the event metadata.
16:40 Tom Brooks: do you provide a change history for role definitions themselves?
16:44 Meera Patel: yes role schema changes are events too and are captured with before/after.
16:50 Dr. Ana Rivera: anything else on data residency? we may require all backups to be US-only.
16:55 Luis Ortega: we can enforce backup-only-in-region for enterprise accounts and add contractual language.
17:05 Priya Shah: would appreciate sample SLA language around audit exports and timelines.
17:10 Jordan Lee: we'll include export SLA language in the follow-up.
17:18 Meera Patel: quick Q from chat: can we stream unsuccessful login attempts to Splunk in near real-time? yes — set up a filter on event.type=auth.fail and forward to HEC.
17:33 Elliot Chen: ok last question: do you sign the whole bundle with our own key if we supply an HSM?
17:38 Luis Ortega: yes, for Private deployments we can use your HSM to sign. for hosted, we support bringing your KMS/HSM via a dedicated signing contract (but requires compliance review).
17:50 Dr. Ana Rivera: thanks — that's all the questions from our side for now. can you summarize next steps?
17:55 Jordan Lee: sure. 1) we'll send SOC2 evidence checklist and chain-of-custody docs, 2) Meera will produce a 30-day signed export sample, 3) Luis will draft KMS key usage doc, 4) schedule Splunk integration demo.
18:15 Priya Shah: thanks everyone.
18:18 Jordan Lee: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links.
18:22 Tom Brooks: bye.
(End of recording — note: final 50 minutes were Q&A and deeper demo artifacts; transcription trimmed here for brevity but full export attached in meeting artifacts.)
